summary.name: Voyager
summary.one_liner: Voyager is an LLM-powered embodied lifelong learning agent for Minecraft that explores, acquires skills as executable code, and improves them through iterative prompting, using GPT-4 via black-box queries.
use_cases: studying lifelong learning in embodied AI agents
building LLM agents that write reusable code skills
summary.what_it_does: Voyager is described as an LLM-powered agent that continuously explores a Minecraft world, acquires diverse skills, and makes discoveries without human intervention. It has three components: an automatic curriculum that maximizes exploration, a growing skill library of executable code for storing and retrieving behaviors, and an iterative prompting mechanism that uses environment feedback, execution errors, and self-verification to improve programs. It interacts with GPT-4 through black-box queries, so no model fine-tuning is needed. The page reports results of 3.3x more unique items, 2.3x longer travel distances, and up to 15.3x faster tech tree milestones versus prior SOTA, and says the skill library transfers to new Minecraft worlds. The authors state the full codebase and prompts are open-sourced.
notable: Skill library of executable code that is stored, retrieved and composed over time
Uses GPT-4 via black-box queries without fine-tuning
Codebase and prompts open-sourced at voyager.minedojo.org
caveats: Results are reported against prior SOTA in Minecraft only; generalization beyond Minecraft is not shown on this page
Depends on access to GPT-4 queries, which the page does not describe as free or paid
